summary: Bound the R19 D3D11 event-query GPU completion wait to 250 ms and exit early on device removal so swapchain teardown cannot hang indefinitely on a stalled/lost GPU while preserving the normal completion-fence path.

C0_RECOVER.evidence: Recovered bookkeeping HEAD c12e56ebd9395c9b8f66fc59ce52513470918b49 after CONVERSION-DX9EX-00454 PASS. Structural extraction remains terminal; 00454 introduced the event-query completion fence and explicitly queued bounded device-loss/stall handling next.

C1_REVIEW.evidence: WaitForSwapchainGpuIdleBeforeDestroy looped while GetData returned S_FALSE with no time or device-loss exit. On a stalled/removed GPU this could block session/reset teardown indefinitely. Existing bounded OpenXR wait policy already uses a 250 ms recovery budget.

C2_IMPLEMENT.evidence: Added SwapchainGpuDrainBudgetMs=250, GetDeviceRemovedReason early exit, elapsed-time cutoff, and verifier assertions while retaining normal End->Flush->GetData-until-S_OK completion ordering.

C3_VALIDATE.evidence: Retry exact SHA passed DX9Ex Active and Domain Isolation; initial policy failure was verifier-only.

red_review.missing_contract: 00454 event-query wait had no bounded exit for persistent S_FALSE and no explicit D3D11 device-removal escape.

references: Microsoft ID3D11DeviceContext::GetData returns S_FALSE while query data is unavailable and must be polled until available on the normal path.
Microsoft ID3D11DeviceContext::Flush is asynchronous; the event query remains the normal completion proof.
